item.title: Vinte e Zinco
item.description:
Written to mark the 25th anniversary of the Carnation Revolution, Vinte e Zinco is a short but quietly devastating novel set in a small Mozambican town on the eve of April 25, 1974 — the day Portugal’s colonial regime collapsed and the world changed, even at its furthest edges.

The title is itself a small act of poetry: “Vinte e Cinco” (the twenty-fifth) becomes “Vinte e Zinco”, replacing cinco (five) with zinco (zinc) — the corrugated metal that roofs the houses of the poor across Africa. In a single word, Mia Couto reframes a date of grand historical significance into something humbler, rooted in the texture of ordinary lives.
